newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria PM says c.bank reserves rise to $1.25 bln.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria PM says c.bank reserves rise to $1.25 bln.

text.p: Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) foreign exchange reserves totalled $1.25 billion at mid-May, up from $1.09 billion on April 21, interim Prime Minister said on Monday.
"Reserves have steadily risen this year...and now amount to $1.25 billion," Stefan Sofianski told a news conference.
A BNB official confirmed reserves have risen in May but declined to elaborate.
Reserves stood at $1.145 billion at end-April, up from $554.3 million a month earlier. They totalled $600.2 million at end-May last year.
Reserves have steadily increased from $415 million at end-January due to net foreign currency purchases by the central bank and proceeds from sell-offs of state-owned firms.
The BNB official said part of the rise in reserves in May was due to proceeds from the sale of Devnya Cement plant to the Bulgarian-Spanish consortium Marvex.
On May 7 Marvex signed an agreement with Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency to buy 70 percent of Devnya Cement for $44.5 million.
The BNB has absorbed higher foreign currency supply which has persisted on the local interbank market from February until last week to boost its reserves.
Dollar supply to the market has come mainly from foreign investors in government securities attracted by high yeilds and pending sell-offs.

Some types of local debt paper, the so called bad debt bonds or ZUNKs, are accepted as means of payment in the privatisation of up to 80 percent of local small and medium companies. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
